Been able to get all of my cats seen whenever needed for emergencies, checkup, vaccines, spay/neuter etc! The key is to call exactly at 7:59 am and DO NOT HANG UP. Stay on hold no matter what. They will eventually answer, even if it takes anywhere from 30 minutes to over an hour. If you truly care about your pet, stick with it and do something else while you wait. I usually put the phone on speaker and use my iPad.

It also helps to already know the menu options so you can select them immediately without waiting through the full recording. I always press 1 for NYC, then 1 for the urgent care hospital in Manhattan or 2 for vaccines, followed by 1 for Bronx or 2 for Brooklyn. Choose the vaccine option even if you are calling for something else because no matter what option you select, they will still ask why you're calling.

This is where many people lose patience, but I have waited as long as 1 hour and 45 minutes and still secured an appointment here. For urgent cases, I have received same day appointments at the ASPCA hospital in Manhattan. The hospital does cost money, but it's truly worth it! You are not paying hundreds of dollars, and they have all the necessary equipment for scans, X rays, and surgeries. It has never been more than $200 for me and that is crazy inexpensive in NYC where I've paid $800 one x-ray and checkup. For ASPCA, appointments are usually scheduled 1 to 2 weeks out sometimes sooner if there is a cancellation. If you call on a Friday, your appointment is the following Friday or one after. It used to be one week but now it's often two.

If you don't want to deal with calling, another easy option is to walk in right when they open. That's also a good way to get an appointment. I have almost always been successful with the phone. The only time I did not get one was when all spots for that day were taken + no cancellations. I simply called back the next day and got an appointment.

The most important thing is to call at 7:59 am. If you call even one minute later, you are automatically out of the running. At that point, staying on hold won't help because they don't answer calls placed after 7:59. Next is to not hang up no matter how long it is because you're already in the queue. They just have to get to your number. If you call at any other time during the day, they won't answer at all, since they already know the calls are for appointments and the available spots have already been taken for that day. You'll have to call again the next morning. I hope this helps those who need it. I cannot stand the thought of animals suffering simply because their owners did not know how to get an appointment.
